newsitem.title: USA: Compaq launches new notebook computer line.
newsitem.headline: Compaq launches new notebook computer line.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp said Tuesday it introduced its Armada 7700 family of notebook computers.

The prices for the Pentium-based mobile computers start at about $5,000 and customers can expand to full desktop functionality, either with a towerable docking station or a convenience base, the company said.

Features of the computer line include integrated AC adapters, Intel Corp's Pentium processors with MMX technology, telephony modems on select models, and dual installation of Microsoft Corp's Windows NT 4.0 and Windows 95.

The new notebooks also include 32 MB Random Access Memory (RAM) standard on two of the three models, expandable to 144 MB; up to 2.1 Gigabyte (GB) hard drives and two 32-bit CardBus slots, Compaq said.
